intent: Acquisition precedes this contract; recorded source and English assessment follows it. Four connected questions are compared separately, without making a hybrid narrative.
context: Root and Hebrew control read all of Exodus4:18–31 in WLC: Moses returns with wife and sons; firstborn death threat precedes the lodging episode; Aaron meets Moses afterward with the same pgš verb. Neither context nor pronoun gender names every participant in24–26.

shared_timing_source: WLC אָז אָמְרָה, adverb plus qatal3fs, not a new wayyiqtol. BDB explicitly lists4:26 as past temporal with perfect; NET reads a retrospective/explanatory comment. Neither establishes mandatory causality or excludes all sequential readings.
rubric: Prioritize actually preserved words and complete literary forms, not manuscript counts, base-text habit or theological comfort
Separate manuscript copying date, translation date, modern edition date and reconstructed reading history
Greek and Aramaic may reflect interpretation or another Hebrew source; neither explanation is proved by agreement
Test strongest alternative: direct early masculine support, feminine coherent reading, ancient angelic agency and connected Greek changes
Compare unchanged-source English for morphology, discourse and avoidable misleading inference; readability alone does not choose ancient Hebrew
Preserve uncertainty about victim, feet possessor, addressee, motive and idiom; gender alone does not identify Moses
Plural morphology does not compel multiple performed circumcisions in the narrative
